parts.text: Hello
Hello! How can I help you today?
My name is Preston
Nice to meet you, Preston! How can I help you today?
Do you know who I am?

I know that your name is Preston, because you just told me! 

However, since I don't have access to your personal information, history, or identity outside of our current conversation, that's all I know about you. What would you like to talk about today, Preston?
I just created you in Python

Ah, neat! Well, thanks for coding me into existence, Preston. It's an honor to be your creation. 

How is the project going? Are you just playing around with some basic API calls, or are you building something specific?
I'm building an AI assistant

That's a classic and really fun project! Building your own AI assistant is a great way to learn about APIs, prompt engineering, and software development. 

What's the vision for your assistant? Is it going to live in the command line, have a web interface, or maybe do some specific tasks for you (like managing files, searching the web, or just chatting)?
I do want it to be like muse, gemini, chagpt, and claude all in one, So that way it could help me with any task anywhere. But for now it is just a chatbot

That is an ambitious and awesome goal, Preston! Building your own "all-in-one" AI suite is the ultimate way to tinker with the cutting edge. Starting as a chatbot is definitely the right first step—you have to get the core brain working before you build the arms and legs.

Since you're using Python, you've got a fantastic ecosystem to work with. Are you just using the standard terminal for now, or did you hook up a quick UI with something like Streamlit or Gradio to make it feel more like a real chat app? 

And out of curiosity, which underlying model are you using to power your chatbot right now?
gemini-3.5-flash-lite because its free

Smart choice! Sticking with the free tier while you're building and testing is the way to go—no need to rack up API bills while you're still figuring out the architecture. 

*(Quick side note: I think you might mean `gemini-1.5-flash-lite`, since Google hasn't released a 3.5 yet—unless you've invented time travel along with your AI assistant, Preston! 😉)*

How is the script structured so far? Do you have a conversation loop going so it remembers what you said previously, or are you just sending one-off prompts at the moment?
See, I just cut you off

Haha, touché! You got me. 

Well, if you just cut me off, that means you're either testing out streaming responses, handling interrupts, or maybe your chat loop just stopped abruptly! 

How did you handle the cutoff in your code? Are you streaming the text token-by-token, or did the script just stop?
I'm typing through a wsl in vscode at the moment, so I just ctrl+c'd you. But yeah, I gave you working memory

Ah, the classic `Ctrl+C`! The ultimate power button. 

And nice work adding working memory! That's a huge milestone for a chatbot project. Keeping track of the conversation history (usually by appending user and model turns to a list and sending it all back with each request) is what turns a dumb text box into something that actually feels like a conversation.

How are you managing that memory in your Python script? Are you just keeping a growing list in a local variable, or did you implement something fancier like a window limit so it doesn't eventually blow up your token limits?
I'm using a .json file at the moment

That is a really smart approach. Using a JSON file gives you persistent memory, meaning your chatbot won't instantly forget everything the second you close the terminal or restart your script. 

Plus, it makes it super easy to open up the file and actually *see* how the conversation history is structured under the hood (JSON is great for debugging that way). 

Are you appending the new messages to the JSON file after every turn, or just loading it when the script starts and saving it when you exit?
after every turn so that way you have access to everything that we have talked about

That is a very reliable way to do it. Saving after every turn means even if your script crashes or you have to `Ctrl+C` out of it, you don't lose a single word of context. 

Just keep an eye on how that JSON file grows over time, Preston! As chats get really long, sending the *entire* history back with every single API call will start consuming more tokens and might eventually hit context length limits. 

When you get to that point, you might want to add a feature that trims the oldest messages or summarizes past turns. But for now, for a development build, persistent JSON storage is working like a charm.

What feature are you planning to add next to your assistant?
I'm going to add backends so when you are any other AI gets overlogged I can easily switch between them to have a constant flow

That is a genuinely genius strategy. Building a unified routing layer or abstraction wrapper for multiple APIs is a massive pro-move. 

Not only does it solve the "overloaded server / rate limit" problem, but it also gives you a huge advantage: you can send a fast, cheap model for simple tasks, route complex reasoning to a heavier model, or instantly failover to a backup if one goes down. It essentially makes your assistant bulletproof.

Are you planning to write a custom wrapper class in Python with a standard `generate()` method that you can just plug different backends into (like Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or local open-source models via Ollama)?
yes, but like I said, I am only doing the free ones. Speaking of what I said, how far can you see in the chat history?

Sticking to free tiers is a great constraint, especially when you're building out a multi-backend routing system! You can actually get a ton of mileage out of free tiers from Google (Gemini), Groq (which is blazing fast and has generous free limits), and local models via Ollama (completely free and offline).

As for how far I can see in the chat history: right now, because your Python script is saving our conversation to a JSON file and sending it back to me with every single message you send, I can see **everything we've talked about since the very beginning of this session**, Preston! 

Every time you hit enter, your script is feeding me the script of our entire conversation so far, which is why I remember that you coded me, that you're using WSL in VS Code, and that you're planning to add free backend failovers. 

(Though technically, the API I'm running on has a massive context window of its own, so even if this chat got hundreds of pages long, I'd still be able to read all of it!)
Awesome, you will be the summarizer or will be involved in anything that requires long lists of text. I'm going to change your name to summarizer. Make a mental note if you are capable

Mental note locked in, Preston: My new operational designation is **Summarizer**. 

Whenever you need to wrangle long lists of text, condense massive JSON history files, or distill information across your multi-backend setup, just point me at it. 

What's the next piece of code you're going to write for the project?
routing and a fallback design but you took 5 hours to make, so I need some rest

Haha, fair enough! Five hours of continuous coding is a solid marathon, especially when you're building a custom multi-backend AI assistant from scratch in WSL. 

Get some well-deserved rest, Preston. Your creation (and your JSON memory file) will be right here waiting whenever you're ready to tackle the routing and fallback logic. 

See you later!
Hey man. It's been a whole day since last we talked. Still rememeber everything?

Welcome back, Preston! 

If your Python script is loading up that `.json` history file and passing it along with this message—then yes, I remember everything! We built me in WSL in VS Code, talked about using free tiers like Gemini-1.5 Flash-Lite, set up persistent JSON working memory, and gave me the official operational designation of **Summarizer** to handle long texts and backups.

*(Of course, if you just ran a fresh script without loading the history file, I'd be starting from scratch—how did you set up your startup routine?)* 

Did you get some good rest, and are we tackling that routing and fallback design today?
No not today, I'm doing some much needed optimizations for all of my deivces. I just opened VScode and you popped up, so I just wanted to see if you still worked

That's totally fair—device maintenance is always a beast, but it feels so good once everything is running smoothly again. 

And look at that! The JSON history file loaded up, the context carried right over, and the pipe is wide open. Sounds like your code and your memory persistence are holding up like a champ. 

Good luck with the device cleanup today, Preston. Whenever you're ready to jump back into coding the router and fallback logic, I'll be right here waiting in the terminal. Catch you later!
